terra.problem: The wall joke does not clearly make sense: a wall along a river is not inherently pointless because someone plans to cross it.
The passage commands the men of valor to cross; it does not say they are the only people who cross.
The passage permits the wives, children and livestock to remain; it does not say everybody else stays home.
The return is tied to both the LORD giving their brothers rest and their taking possession of the land, not just to rest. The passage does not identify a particular day.
The claim that Moses discusses wisdom elsewhere in the sermon needs a reference, since it is outside this passage.
The passage permits the men to return; it does not order them to go home.
Calling Joshua Moses' attendant is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The explanation invents what Moses would have said if the plan depended on counting soldiers.
The claim that nobody tells someone not to fear a kingdom that has surrendered is an unsupported absolute.
Moses asks to cross over and see the land, but does not say he wants to see it with Israel.
Identifying both defeated kings as Sihon and Og requires a reference to the earlier passages; Sihon is not named in this passage.
The LORD tells Moses to look in four directions and see the land; the passage does not say he can see all of it.
Calling this Moses' 'last stretch' adds a timeframe that this passage does not give.
Saying Moses is recounting the whole journey overstates what the text establishes.
Saying Moses has 'just' handed out the land makes the earlier allotment sound like it has just happened.
Rebuilding does not necessarily mean something was knocked down; that assertion is too definite.
